text:
marta: Heads-up — seeing a spike in GPU eviction churn in ap-southeast1 over the last ~2h. Eviction rate up ~5% vs baseline, lots of tiny pods getting preempted by larger reserved jobs.
cheng: yep, logs show a bunch of taint:gpu_reserve:NoSchedule flips + scheduler backfill attempts that leave tiny free fragments.
sam: interesting — looks like hetero GPU shapes + strict binpack policy is causing fragmentation. small pods can't fit into leftovers, so the scheduler keeps evicting to reshuffle.
tanvi: any immediate mitigation we can do? customers are noticing latency on batch jobs.
marta: quick plan: bump warm-pool and relax strict binpack for low-priority namespaces for 30m, monitor. Also consider temporarily marking some large reserved nodes as not-eligible for preempt to stop thrash.
cheng: I can run a conservative change to scheduler config: lower packStrictness from 0.95 -> 0.85 for a test cohort. sample patch:
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap gpu-scheduler-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"packStrictness":"0.85"}}'
```
sam: nice. Also scale warmpool: bump to +20 warmpool replicas in ap-southeast1 to give the tiny pods a landing pad.
tanvi: I'll do the warm-pool scale now for the low-prio test namespace (ns: batch-scratch).
```bash
kubectl -n infra-scale scale deploy/warm-pool-apse --replicas=60 # from 40 -> 60
```
marta: thanks. Cheng, can we also relax node taint enforcement briefly? maybe add toleration to the test namespace instead of touching nodes.
cheng: safer to add toleration. patch for namespace:
```bash
kubectl -n batch-scratch patch deploy --all -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"gpu_reserve","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule","tolerationSeconds":1800}]}}}}'
```
tanvi: started step 1 (scale warm-pool). Will report back in ~5m. :thumbsup:
devops-bot: [alert] ap-southeast1 warm-pool scaling triggered by tanvi. Request ID: r-9f3b.
sam: after warm-pool and tolerations: if eviction rate drops, we keep changes for 30m and then revert. If not, rollback and open a deeper scheduler investigation runbook.
marta: agreed. Follow-up action items: 1) monitor eviction/fit-failure metrics (cheng) 2) revert packStrictness if no improvement (cheng) 3) adjust reserved-node annotation plan (sam) 4) post-mortem if regression continues (marta).
cheng: monitoring dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/evicts/gpu-evictions?orgId=1 (watch the "fit_failures" and "preempt_count" panels).
tanvi: warm-pool scaled to 60, rolling toleration patch applied to batch-scratch. observing pod startup spike now.
devops-bot: [info] warm-pool scale complete. new size=60.
marta: good. Give it 20m, then decide roll-forward. thanks all.
sam: if this helps, follow-up we should consider a scheduler heuristic that prefers filling warm-pools first when small fragment islands exist. filing RFC after triage. :bookmark:
